transcript:
This message comes from Synchrony Bank, who can help you get your do-nothing savings off the couch and working hard.
No more sleeping late and needing all the chips. Time to start earning your keep in a big way,
with their high-yield savings account that has a great rate, easy access to your funds, and no monthly fees or minimum balance requirements.
Put your lazy savings to work. Go to Synchrony.com/NPR. Remember FDIC.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
An outgoing Republican House member has brought articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
As NPR's Barbra Sprounter reports, this is up a vote in the House within two days.
Congressman Thomas Massey has long been a critic of Secretary Hegseth.
The Kentucky Republican first tried to bring an impeachment resolution ahead of the midterm elections,
but House Speaker Mike Johnson called an early recess to avoid the vote.
Massey's impeachment resolution lists eight charges against Hegseth, including illegally waging war against Iran,
overseeing extrajudicial killings in the Caribbean, and suppressing free speech.
The argument here is that he's broken laws and he's violated the Constitution.
There will likely be sufficient votes in the House to impeach,
but it's unlikely to clear the higher Senate threshold for convicting and removing Hegseth from office,
which requires two-thirds of the Senate.
Barbra Sprounter, NPR News, Washington.
Shares in the chipmaker NVIDIA dropped more than four percent today.
This comes after the company announced over the weekend that it's investigating its CEO,
who had an affair with a woman who was allegedly recruited to spy for China.
NPR's John Ruich has more.
NVIDIA shares took a beating while the rest of the market bounced back after losses last week.
The company said on Sunday it's investigating CEO Jensen Huang after reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
But for now, Huang is still in charge of the $4.3 trillion company that he co-founded more than 30 years ago.
The New York Times has reported that U.S. intelligence agencies believed Huang was having an affair with a Chinese woman
at a Singapore-based company that had bought Nvidia chips and that she was recruited by China's top spy agency.
NPR has not independently confirmed the reporting.
John Ruich, NPR News.
The annual United Nations Climate Summit, also known as COP31, is underway in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya.
And PSIDIL Al-Shalchi reports nearly 70,000 people are expected to attend the two-week event.
The U.N.'s climate chief Simon Steele called on nations to treat COP31 as an implementation summit
that faces the reality of global warming overshooting 1.5 degrees Celsius or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit head-on.
He called countries to slash red tape on climate finance and turned clean energy pledges into immediate action.
Exceeding warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius increases the risk of dangerous heat waves, water and food shortages,
and crossing irreversible tipping points like collapsing ice sheets.
The U.N. will not attend the summit for a second year in a row and is set to soon leave the larger framework
that organizes international climate negotiations.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Antalya.
Wall Street sharply higher by the close, all three major indices up more than 2 percent.
The Dow gained 1,104 points, the NASDAQ up 673, the S&P 500 up 173.
You're listening to NPR News.
British comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced to ten and a half years in prison
for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.
A jury found him guilty of attacking four of six accusers with allegations dating back to 2004.
Prosecutors say Brand abused his fame to access women,
and the assaults happened during a time when his comedy career was taking off.
He maintains his innocence, saying all encounters were consensual.
Brand, known for his outrageous routines and battles with addictions,
will have to serve at least seven years before he can be considered for parole.
M. John Harrison's post-apocalyptic sci-fi novel "The End of Everything" has won this year's Booker Prize.
The award goes to the best fiction that's published in the UK and Ireland.
As NPR's Andrew Limbong reports, this is the first time the prize has gone to a science fiction book.
Gabby Wood, the chief executive of the Booker Prize Foundation, said in a statement that
while past Booker Prize authors have borrowed from sci-fi,
M. John Harrison is the first author to emerge out of that world.
"He is a genuinely original thinker, a genre-defying writer who takes ideas seriously."
"The End of Everything" follows a man who lives along the southern coast of Kent, England,
spending his time looking for artifacts when he comes across a shape-shifting object.
The novel takes place during a slow-burning, sort of, alien invasion.
At 81 years old, Harrison is the oldest writer to win the prize.
"The End of Everything" is his 13th novel.
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Republican Rep. Thomas Massey files eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
NVIDIA shares fall over four percent after CEO Jensen Huang is investigated over alleged foreign spy affair
UN Climate Summit COP31 opens in Antalya, Turkey, with nearly 70,000 attendees expected
Wall Street rallies sharply, with the Dow up 1,104 points and the S&P 500 up 173
Comedian Russell Brand sentenced to ten and a half years in prison for rape and sexual assault
M. John Harrison's sci-fi novel "The End of Everything" wins the Booker Prize, a first for the genre
